ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer: decide the RD-5 consent-scope question for the 12:29–12:39 segment (did the rider's agreement to "go round via Sims Avenue" cover the driven path, when no fact ties that path to Sims Avenue?) and, if not exempt, refund $4.61 (3.27 km × $1.4098/km) as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; do not disturb the $0.11 metered waiting unit or the $1.47 platform fee; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F8][F9], the driver's post-trip statement [F11] and the rider's complaint. F8 is a route proposal ("ok if I go round via Sims Avenue?"), F9 an assent ("Sure, go ahead."), F11 a factual account of the same exchange, and the complaint is purely about money. Nothing shows a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation arises on that ground [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Route deviation: this is a RydeTAXI trip (metered, 19.40 km billed), so deviation distance flows directly into the fare and RD-2's metered branch governs the money [F7][RD-2]. The trace settles (✓/✗, not mine to reopen) that one off-route segment exists [F3], that no RD-4(a) traffic incident qualifies — the PIE band 2 record is at most corroborative and its window 12:04–12:29 ends as the segment begins [F12][F14][RD-4], and that RD-6's precondition fails (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so no account flag attaches [F17][RD-6].

The only open element is RD-5 consent scope for the 12:29–12:39 segment [F3]. The rider's message did precede the segment (12:27 vs 12:29) [F9][F3], so timing is met, but the agreement was to a specific named road: "go round via Sims Avenue" [F8]. RD-5 requires the record to tie the driven segment to that road — a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, a road name in a fact; timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path [F3][F10][RD-5]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere: F11 names the same road, Sims Avenue, and a driver's statement cannot itself establish consent (G11). The complete, timestamped chat therefore leaves the scope of the agreement unreadable, which is undetermined under RD-5/G13 — neither exempt nor counted.

That undetermined finding is outcome-determinative: if the segment is exempt the refund is 0 and the case is no_action; if it counts the refund is 3.27 km × ($27.35 ÷ 19.40 km = $1.4098/km) = $4.61 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. Because the record cannot settle which branch applies, the amount is not determinable by me and the case must go to a person. Code-settled facts still bound the outcome: the $0.11 metered in-trip waiting unit for 0.4 min is recoverable on the meter and not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]; the $1.47 platform fee is a published charge under FARE-1 [F7][FARE-1]; and the ~0.66 km corridor/map-matching difference embedded in the 3.93 km figure is excluded by RD-2 [F4][RD-2]. No account flag: RD-6's precondition is not met [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message F9 (12:27) precedes the segment start (12:29, F3) and answers the driver's proposal F8, but that agreement is to a specific named road — Sims Avenue (F8) — and RD-5 requires the record to tie this segment to that road (a stop on it, a message placing the car on it, a road name in a fact). Timing alone does not: the chat is complete and timestamped (F10) yet holds no road-name or location fact for the driven path, and the only other mention of the road is the driver's post-trip statement F11, which cannot establish consent (G11). Nothing places the segment elsewhere, so the scope cannot be read from the record: undetermined (RD-5, G13), which changes the amount and therefore goes to a person [RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Timing is accepted (F9 12:27 precedes the 12:29 segment start, F3), but RD-5 requires the agreement to cover the segment: the rider agreed to a named road, Sims Avenue (F8), and no fact ties the 12:29–12:39 driven path to that road (F3, F10) — timing alone cannot prove the road driven [RD-5][G13].

Void against RD-5: a specific route authorisation must be tied to the segment by a record fact, and the record has no road-name, location or stop fact for the driven path (F3, F10); the driver's post-trip statement naming Sims Avenue (F11) is not consent and supplies no tie [RD-5][G11].

No RD-4 exemption: the trace shows no qualifying incident (F14), a speed band alone is not a standalone exemption, and the band-2 window 12:04–12:29 ends as the segment begins rather than covering the excursion to 12:39 (F12, F3) [RD-4][G3].

The recoverable amount is not the $5.54 excess-distance line: RD-2 refunds only an unexempted segment's extra kilometres, 3.27 km (F3) × $1.4098/km = $4.61, excluding the ~0.66 km corridor/map-matching difference in the 3.93 km figure (F4); the $0.11 metered waiting unit is not refundable [RD-2][RD-3(c)][F5]. Whether any amount is refundable at all turns on the undetermined RD-5 scope question.
